findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0355: References to Unauthorized Database Access through Content Providers
findings.explanation:
A content provider is exported with no permission: any installed app can query it. If it is public by design, accept it with a reason.
sync/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:7: provider app.pennyjar.sync.ReceiptsProvider; exported: yes (android:exported is set)

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0357: References to Oversharing of File-Based Content Providers
findings.explanation:
A content provider is exported with no permission: any installed app can query it. If it is public by design, accept it with a reason.
sync/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:7: provider app.pennyjar.sync.ReceiptsProvider; exported: yes (android:exported is set)

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0364: Exported And Unprotected Activities That Expose Sensitive Functionality
findings.explanation:
HelpActivity is exported without a permission and lets any app or web link load an arbitrary URL into a WebView whose JS bridge returns the session token.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:32: Exported with no android:permission.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpBridge.kt:14: Sensitive data reachable through it.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0327: References to APIs for Event-Bound Biometric Authentication
findings.explanation:
The biometric app lock calls BiometricPrompt.authenticate without a CryptoObject and no key uses setUserAuthenticationRequired, so unlocking relies only on the callback.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/BiometricGate.kt:51: Event-bound authentication.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/BiometricGate.kt:47: Success callback alone unlocks the app.

findings.title: MASWE-0024: Sensitive Data Accessible After Session Termination
findings.explanation:
Sign-out clears the database, prefs and caches but not the plaintext CSV backup in public Documents, so expense data stays on the device after the session ends.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/backup/AutoBackupWorker.kt:21: Backup location not removed by clearLocalData().

findings.title: MASWE-0042: Latest Platform Version Not Targeted
findings.explanation:
targetSdk is 34. Since 2026-08-31, Google Play accepts new phone and tablet apps and updates only if they target API 36 or higher (rule checked 2026-11-23).
app/build.gradle.kts:14: targetSdk 34

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0272: Identify Dependencies with Known Vulnerabilities in the Android Project
findings.explanation:
com.google.code.gson:gson:2.8.5 is in the affected range of 1 OSV advisory: GHSA-4jrv-ppp4-jm57/CVE-2022-25647. OSV Maven data downloaded 2026-11-25T19:34:24.991Z (published Mon, 23 Nov 2026 21:33:52 GMT). 9 of the other dependencies with exact versions match no OSV advisory, but 2 declarations have no version Ward can read (see evidence). Check those, and transitive dependencies, with a Gradle-aware scanner. OSV Maven data downloaded 2026-11-25T19:34:24.991Z (published Mon, 23 Nov 2026 21:33:52 GMT).
gradle/libs.versions.toml:11: version 2.8.5
sync/build.gradle.kts:37: implementation (catalog libs.gson) in module sync
app/build.gradle.kts:45: androidx.compose.ui:ui: no version (a BOM or constraint may set it)
app/build.gradle.kts:46: androidx.compose.material3:material3: no version (a BOM or constraint may set it)

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0274: Dependencies with Known Vulnerabilities in the App's SBOM
findings.explanation:
No SBOM in the project, but the declared Gson 2.8.5 is in the affected range of GHSA-4jrv-ppp4-jm57 (CVE-2022-25647) per Ward's dependency analyzer.
gradle/libs.versions.toml:11: Vulnerable Gson version.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0339: SQL Injection in Content Providers
findings.explanation:
The exported ReceiptsProvider passes the URI's last path segment into a raw SQL string for merchant queries.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ReceiptsProvider.kt:40: Untrusted URI segment passed on.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ReceiptQueries.kt:20: Concatenated into SQL.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0394: Missing Input Validation in Custom URL Scheme Handlers
findings.explanation:
HelpActivity reads the 'page' query parameter from the pennyjar://help deep link and loads it in the JS-bridged WebView without any host allowlist.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:40: Unvalidated URL parameter.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:43: Used directly as the WebView URL.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0398: References to WebViewClient URL Loading Handlers
findings.explanation:
HelpActivity assigns a bare WebViewClient() with no shouldOverrideUrlLoading allowlist, so the bridged WebView navigates to any URL, including ones passed via the deep link.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:27: No URL restriction on a WebView exposing a JS bridge.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0204: Insecure Random API Usage
findings.explanation:
Share-link tokens, which grant access to a month's expense report, are generated with java.util.Random.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/share/ShareLinks.kt:11: Non-cryptographic PRNG.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/share/ShareLinks.kt:15: Used to build the access token.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0232: Broken Symmetric Encryption Modes
findings.explanation:
Private expense notes are encrypted with AES in ECB mode.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteCipher.kt:9: ECB mode transformation.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0208: Insufficient Key Sizes
findings.explanation:
The hardcoded note key is 16 bytes (AES-128), which the test treats as insufficient; the Keystore session key is 256-bit.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteKeys.kt:13: 16-byte key used as AES-128.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0212: Use of Hardcoded Cryptographic Keys in Code
findings.explanation:
The AES key that encrypts users' private expense notes is a hardcoded byte array wrapped in SecretKeySpec.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteKeys.kt:8: Hardcoded key bytes.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteKeys.kt:13: Hardcoded bytes used as the note encryption key.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0287: Runtime Storage of Unencrypted Data via the SharedPreferences API
findings.explanation:
CredentialStore saves the user's email and plaintext password in SharedPreferences when 'Remember me' is on (the default).
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/CredentialStore.kt:12: Password stored unencrypted in SharedPreferences.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/AuthRepository.kt:20: Called on every remembered sign-in.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0233: Hardcoded HTTP URLs
findings.explanation:
Receipt thumbnails are downloaded from a hardcoded http:// URL with the bearer token attached by AuthInterceptor, and cleartext is allowed by the network security config.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/Endpoints.kt:6: Cleartext image endpoint.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/ui/ThumbnailCache.kt:25: Used for real downloads.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0235: Android App Configurations Allowing Cleartext Traffic
findings.explanation:
The network security config's base-config permits cleartext traffic for every domain.
app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:3: base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0282: Unsafe Custom Trust Evaluation
findings.explanation:
UploadClient uses a custom X509TrustManager whose checkServerTrusted is empty and getAcceptedIssuers returns an empty array, accepting any certificate for receipt image uploads (with the bearer token).
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/UploadClient.kt:19: Trust-all checkServerTrusted.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/UploadClient.kt:27: Installed on the upload client.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0283: Incorrect Implementation of Server Hostname Verification
findings.explanation:
UploadClient's HostnameVerifier always returns true.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/UploadClient.kt:28: Hostname verification disabled.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0226: Debuggable Flag Enabled in the AndroidManifest
findings.explanation:
The release build type sets isDebuggable to true.
app/build.gradle.kts:23: isDebuggable = true

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0227: Debugging Enabled for WebViews
findings.explanation:
WebView debugging is enabled unconditionally at app start, without checking FLAG_DEBUGGABLE.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/PennyJarApp.kt:45: Unconditional WebView debugging.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0334: Native Code Exposed Through WebViews
findings.explanation:
HelpActivity enables JavaScript and adds a JS bridge whose sessionToken() returns the user's API session token; the page URL comes unvalidated from an exported deep link, so any website can read the token.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:23: JavaScript enabled.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:28: Bridge registered on the WebView.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpBridge.kt:14: Session token exposed to JavaScript.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:43: Loads an attacker-chosen URL.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0254: Dangerous App Permissions
findings.explanation:
ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION is requested although location is only read in the foreground when the user taps 'Tag place'; FINE location is requested where a city needs only coarse.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:8: Background location declared.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/ui/AddExpenseScreen.kt:81: Background location requested with no background feature.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0318: References to SDK APIs Known to Handle Sensitive User Data
findings.explanation:
Mixpanel's identify() is called with the user's email, and expense events send merchant names, without checking the analytics consent the app asks for.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/analytics/Analytics.kt:14: Email sent to Mixpanel as the user ID.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/analytics/Analytics.kt:22: Merchant sent with each expense event.

findings.title: MASWE-0072: Inadequate Privacy Policy
findings.explanation:
A privacy policy link or text is in the app. Ward doesn't read the policy: check that it matches what the app collects and the Data safety answers.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/settings/SettingsScreen.kt:44: privacy policy
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/settings/SettingsScreen.kt:103: privacy policy
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/settings/SettingsScreen.kt:105: privacy policy

findings.title: MASWE-0076: Lack of Proper Data Management Controls
findings.explanation:
Users can create an account here, but Ward found no way to delete it: no delete-account code, text or link in the scanned files. Google Play requires apps that allow account creation to offer an in-app path to delete the account and its data; a link to a web page counts (rule checked 2026-11-23, https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13327111).
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/AuthRepository.kt:25: account creation
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/LoginScreen.kt:85: account creation
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/LoginScreen.kt:96: account creation
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/LoginScreen.kt:99: account creation
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ApiClient.kt:35: account creation

findings.title: MASWE-0078: Inadequate or Ambiguous User Consent Mechanisms
findings.explanation:
The app asks for consent to usage statistics, but Analytics never checks ConsentStore: tracking starts at app open and continues after 'No thanks'.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/PennyJarApp.kt:53: Tracked before any consent is given.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/analytics/Analytics.kt:10: No consent check before tracking.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0202: References to APIs and Permissions for Accessing External Storage
findings.explanation:
WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is declared (with requestLegacyExternalStorage) and AutoBackupWorker writes an unencrypted CSV of all expenses (date, amount, merchant, city) to the public Documents directory.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:9: Shared-storage write permission declared.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/backup/AutoBackupWorker.kt:21: Backup directory is in public external storage.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/backup/AutoBackupWorker.kt:24: Financial records written there as plaintext CSV.

findings.title: MASWE-0004: Sensitive Data Hardcoded in the App Package
findings.explanation:
A helpdesk API bearer token is hardcoded in the app and sent from the device.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/support/SupportClient.kt:35: Hardcoded helpdesk API token.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0216: Sensitive Data Not Excluded From Backup
findings.explanation:
Backup is on (android:allowBackup="true") and there are no backup rules (dataExtractionRules, fullBackupContent), so every app file goes into cloud backups and device transfers.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:13: android:allowBackup="true"

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0231: References to Logging APIs
findings.explanation:
ApiClient installs OkHttp's HttpLoggingInterceptor at BODY level in all builds, which logs login/register request bodies (email, password), Authorization headers and responses with session tokens.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ApiClient.kt:25: Full request/response bodies and headers go to the log.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0262: References to Backup Configurations Not Excluding Sensitive Data
findings.explanation:
Backup is on (android:allowBackup="true") and there are no backup rules (dataExtractionRules, fullBackupContent), so every app file goes into cloud backups and device transfers.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:13: android:allowBackup="true"
